transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I’m not wasting your time with this, I know it's probably not a huge deal, but... I came in because I’m just so, so tired lately. I'm trying really hard to keep up, but I can barely get through a shift at work right now. 

It kind of feels like... well, like my body is filled with wet sand, if that makes sense? And even when I do rest, it doesn’t really bring me back. I mean, I'm doing my best to push through it and be a good employee, I promise, but... is that the right kind of thing to come here for?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities?

Oh, um... I guess maybe a little? I really try to keep up with everything, I promise, I don't want to just sit around being lazy or anything. But... well, yeah, things I usually love doing... like cooking for myself, or playing my guitar, or going on a hike... even just going over to my family’s place. It all just feels kind of... flat right now? 

Like, I’m just going through the motions and pretending to care so I don't bring anyone else down. I mean, I still try to do those things, because I want to be good company and normal for them. I really hope that doesn't sound awful of me to say. Is it normal to feel like that when you're just really exhausted?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the time lately?

Um... I guess, maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... yeah, I suppose I have been feeling a bit down. Not hopeless, really, just... kind of heavy, I guess? 

I try to keep a smile on my face at work and around my family, because I don't want to be a burden or make anyone worry. I know everyone has bad days, and I'm sure this is just a phase I need to push through. I mean, it's okay to feel a little sad sometimes, right? I'm really trying my best not to let it get to me.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your energy levels or an increase in fatigue, even when you haven't been doing much physically taxing?

Yeah, um... like I mentioned when we first started talking, that's really the main thing I've been struggling with. I'm just so, so exhausted. 

I know standing at a register all day isn't exactly, you know, heavy manual labor, so I feel a little silly complaining about it. I really should be able to handle it better. But even on my days off, when I'm barely doing anything physical at all, I still have that heavy, wet sand feeling I was telling you about. It's like... no matter how much I sleep or rest on the couch, I just don't bounce back. 

I'm really trying my hardest to push through it and not let it affect my job, I promise. I hope I'm explaining it okay... does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way — the sadness, the lack of interest, and the fatigue — have these been happening for more than a couple of weeks?

Um... yeah, it's... it's definitely been more than a couple of weeks. I'm sorry, I probably should have come in sooner instead of letting it get like this. I really thought I could just fix it myself if I tried hard enough. But... I think this really low, empty part has lasted about four months now? 

It kind of settled in long after that first rush of energy I had at work passed. I was doing so great for a little bit, getting everything done and feeling really on top of things, but then... yeah, it's been about four months of just feeling completely drained. I kept hoping I could just snap out of it so I wouldn't be such a drag on my coworkers and my family. I really hope it doesn't make me sound weak that I haven't been able to just push past it yet. Does four months sound like a normal amount of time to be stuck in a rut like this?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently — like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual?

Um... well, my appetite has been a little all over the place, I guess. I really try to make sure I'm eating enough so I have energy for my shifts, I know how important that is. But... lately, I just kind of forget? 

Or when I do try to eat, it just feels like... I don't know, like I'm chewing on cardboard. It's not that I'm trying to lose weight on purpose or anything, I promise. But I did notice that my work pants are fitting a lot looser than they used to. I feel bad because my mom made a comment about me looking too thin, and I hate making her worry. I should probably try harder to force myself to eat, right? Is it okay that I just haven't had much of an appetite?
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't seem to sit still and feel restless?

Um... well, it's kind of been both, depending on when you look at it. I hope that's an okay answer. 

Like... a while back, when I had that burst of energy I mentioned, I couldn't sit still at all. I was constantly pacing around the store, straightening shelves, just... moving all the time. I thought I was being super helpful, you know? Keeping busy. But lately... it's the opposite. 

I'm sorry, I really try not to let it show, but even just walking to the bus stop or... or trying to answer a customer's question, it just feels so incredibly slowed down. Like I'm moving through molasses, and my body just feels so heavy. I try to put on a smile and move faster so people don't think I'm lazy, but it's really hard. Does that make sense? Is it normal for it to change from one extreme to the other like that?
Before this current four-month period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt this same kind of low mood, fatigue, and loss of interest that lasted for weeks at a time?

Um... no, I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I'm really trying to think back, but I don't remember ever feeling quite this bad for this long before. 

I mean, sure, everyone gets sad sometimes, right? Like, if I had a bad week at work or something, I might have felt a little down or tired for a few days. But I always tried really hard to just bounce back quickly so I wouldn't bother anyone with it. I've never had it drag on for months where I just couldn't shake it off like I can't right now. 

I'm sorry if that's not very helpful... I just really don't think I've ever let myself get stuck in a rut like this before. Does that mean this is just a one-time thing, hopefully? I really want to believe I can just get back to being my normal self soon.
